newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy March CPI seen falling to 2.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy March CPI seen falling to 2.3 pct.

text.p: Italy's March consumer price index (CPI) inflation is set to fall slightly to an annual rate of 2.3 percent compared to a year-on-year rate of 2.4 percent in February, according to a survey of economists.
The March monthly CPI rate is expected to show a rise of 0.2 percent after a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent in February.
Economists said that the fall in the inflation rate will come from the revision of telecom tariffs, the rise in the value of the dollar and lower seasonal prices.
Eleven Italian cities will report their preliminary CPI data on Thursday March 20 and Friday March 21, while the national official data for Italy will be published on April 7.

Economists pointed out there were a number of factors restraining inflation such as the small rise in car prices by carmaker Fiat of just 1.6 percent, and small price rises in medicines, cigarettes and other tariffs such as trains, gas and motorway tolls.

Economist Pio Gregori at NatWest said that the calculation of this month's CPI was more complex as there were contrasting effects and diverse factors. He pointed out that there will be a reduction in prices of fruit and vegetables due to good weather, especially in the centre and north of Italy.

Alfredo Granata of Banca di Roma said the inflationary tendency remains subdued, while Marco Pianelli of Nomura said that inflation will be contained by sluggish demand in most areas apart from car sales, which were boosted by a car buying incentive scheme.
